headword: {異常|いじょう}{気象|きしょう}

definitions.explanation: Weather conditions that deviate significantly from historical norms, such as record heatwaves, unusually heavy rainfall, or unprecedented cold spells.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{異常|いじょう}{気象|きしょう}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There has been a lot of extreme weather this year.

examples.japanese: {異常|いじょう}{気象|きしょう}の{原因|げんいん}は{温暖|おんだん}{化|か}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that global warming is the cause of extreme weather.

examples.japanese: {異常|いじょう}{気象|きしょう}による{農作物|のうさくぶつ}への{被害|ひがい}が{深刻|しんこく}になっている。
examples.english: Damage to crops from extreme weather is becoming serious.

notes:
USAGE:
A frequently used term in news broadcasts and newspaper articles. Japan experiences various forms of extreme weather including {猛暑|もうしょ} (intense heat), {豪雨|ごうう} (heavy rain), and {大雪|おおゆき} (heavy snow).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {異常|いじょう}{気象|きしょう}が{続|つづ}く (extreme weather continues)
- {異常|いじょう}{気象|きしょう}による{被害|ひがい} (damage from extreme weather)
- {異常|いじょう}{気象|きしょう}の{原因|げんいん} (cause of abnormal weather)
- {異常|いじょう}{気象|きしょう}が{増|ふ}えている (extreme weather is increasing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {天災|てんさい}: natural disaster — a broader term including earthquakes and tsunamis
- {気候|きこう}{変動|へんどう}: climate change — refers to long-term trends, not individual events
